title: Counting elements satisfying a predicate
statement: Let $q$ be a natural number and let $p$ be a decidable predicate on $\{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}$. The number of indices $i$ in this set for which $p(i)$ holds equals the number of true instances of $p$ in the list $0,1,\ldots,q-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a decidable predicate on the indices from $0$ to $q-1$
